name: Kumano Kodo Kohechi (熊野古道 小辺路)
why: The pilgrims' shortcut from the temple town of Koyasan to Kumano Hongu: four days over three passes above 1,000 m, sleeping in remote mountain villages.
book: Book every night before you start: Omata, Miura-guchi (only two inns, check it first) and Totsukawa onsen; partial bookings are not accepted. Closed mid-December to mid-March except Hatenashi pass. A luggage shuttle runs on this route. Buses are rare, so you must be able to walk each day in full.
water: Fill up at each inn: there are no shops or springs you can count on between the villages. Carry 2 litres and lunch every day.
dangers: Steeper and more remote than the Nakahechi: for experienced walkers only.
Rain, wind and thick fog on the high passes; washouts near Obako peak cause detours, follow the signs.
Snow on the passes in winter: the route is officially closed then.
Mamushi vipers, hornets, leeches and ticks in the forest (see the tourism bureau's safety tips).
turnaround: If the weather is bad at Omata or Miura-guchi, do not start the pass: wait a day or take the bus round.

points.name: Koyasan
points.note: The temple town on its mountain plateau; sleep in a temple lodging the night before. Day 1 crosses Mizugamine to Omata: 17 km, 6-8 h.

points.name: Omata
points.note: Night 1 in a small village on the Kawazu-Koya road. Day 2 is the hardest: 14.5 km over Obako to Miura-guchi.

points.name: Obako pass
points.note: The pass under Obako peak, 1,344 m, with a shelter hut. The north side is wide and gentle, the south side narrow and steep.

points.name: Miura-guchi
points.note: Night 2. Day 3 crosses Miura pass, then follows Route 425 down the Nishi-gawa for the last 8 km to Totsukawa: 18 km in all.

points.name: Totsukawa onsen
points.note: Night 3 in a hot spring village. Day 4 climbs straight from Hotel Subaru to Hatenashi pass through hillside hamlets.

points.name: Yakio, on the Kumano river
points.note: The foot of the Hatenashi pass trail at the Yakio bus stop. Kumano Hongu Taisha is an hour's walk on by the Kumano river, or a short bus ride.
